races.name: British Stallion Studs EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes (Bands C And D) (EBF Restricted Qualifer) (GBB)

runners_data.name: Red Spells Danger
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with clear class edge on ratings, consistent RPRs in 70s make him the form standard despite being winless
runners_data.comment: 0-6 but he's been consistent and sets a clear standard back on turf; big player
runners_data.spotlight: 0-6 but he's recorded RPRs in the 70s in all of his runs, including when second at Catterick (7f, good) and Southwell (7f, AW) this spring; sets a clear standard back on turf and he has shaped as though this drop to 6f could suit.

runners_data.name: Tip Foster
runners_data.note: Recently gelded prominent type who ran well for a long way on debut before weakening, step forward expected
runners_data.comment: Promising third on Pontefract debut and has possibilities if he can build on that
runners_data.spotlight: Gelded son of Dream Ahead; weak 18-1 at Pontefract (6f, good to soft) last month but ran well for a long way before finishing 4l third behind a useful prospect; that was a promising start and has possibilities if he can build on that.

runners_data.name: Soda
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner who finished well at Pontefract, needs honest pace to be effective from the back
runners_data.comment: Showed ability at Catterick but she needs a big step forward on this drop in trip
runners_data.spotlight: 4,000euros yearling; sister to 7f/1m winner Crossford (including Hong Kong; RPR 97), half-sister to four winners at 7f-1m4f; 18-1, came from off the pace to finish third of six on recent Catterick debut (7f, good) but was beaten about 5l and needs a big step forward on this drop in trip.

runners_data.name: Highfield Jewel
runners_data.note: Lightly raced 4yo returning after 106 days, previous form too modest to suggest readiness for this grade
runners_data.comment: Well held in two runs at Southwell during the winter and has plenty to find on her return
runners_data.spotlight: 4yo who was well held in two runs at Southwell (7f/6f) this winter, showing modest form; has plenty to find on her return and handicaps look the way forward after this.

runners_data.name: Rousham
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with valid excuse last time when hampered at crucial stage, capable of better
runners_data.comment: Ran better than the bare facts at Doncaster and he's one to keep an eye on
runners_data.spotlight: Well held at massive prices in two runs this spring but he wasn't far away when he got badly hampered at a crucial stage at Doncaster (6f, good to firm) last month; showed definite signs of ability in that race and he's a half-brother to three sprint winners; one to keep an eye on.

runners_data.name: Sparkling Wine
runners_data.note: Returns after 387-day absence, needs major improvement but Michael Dods stable in good form recently
runners_data.comment: Didn't show much in sole 2yo run (April) and needs major improvement on her comeback
runners_data.spotlight: 80-1 and outpaced before finishing eighth of 12 on Beverley debut (5f, good) last April; returns after long absence and she needs major improvement upped in trip.

runners_data.name: Ndoto
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with modest AW form, needs significant step forward to be competitive here
runners_data.comment: Beaten about 7l in two AW runs and needs a transformation on turf debut
runners_data.spotlight: Beaten about 7l on Wolverhampton debut (6f) in March and same outcome in another small-field event at Southwell (7f) later that month; still early days but she needs a transformation on this switch to turf.

races.paceDynamic: Red Spells Danger will lead or track the early pace with Tip Foster and Rousham also showing prominent tendencies, creating a modest gallop in this small field. The hold-up horses Soda and Ndoto will need the pace to be honest enough to close into, but with limited pace pressure expected, the tempo may not be searching enough. This race shape clearly favours the prominent runners who can position close to Red Spells Danger and have first run on the field, as the hold-up horses may find themselves with too much ground to make up in the straight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Red Spells Danger sets a steady gallop without serious pressure early
scenarios.body: The race becomes tactical and those tracking the leader get first run, while hold-up horses are left flat-footed. Red Spells Danger's superior ratings tell as Tip Foster and Rousham struggle to match his class.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent runners go faster than expected or Red Spells Danger weakens
scenarios.body: Soda can use her proven ability to close strongly as she did at Pontefract, with Ndoto also benefiting from increased pace. The race sets up perfectly for closers to sweep past tiring leaders.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Upset from Improvers
scenarios.trigger: If the form horses disappoint and lesser-rated runners step forward
scenarios.body: Rousham benefits from the interference excuse at Doncaster last time and runs to a higher level, while Highfield Jewel finds improvement returning from a break. The modest pace suits horses needing to find their best form.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Longshot Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If the market leaders all underperform on the day
scenarios.body: Sparkling Wine returns vastly improved from her long absence under Michael Dods' guidance, taking advantage of a weak pace scenario. The step up to 6f suits better than her 5f debut effort.

watchPoints.text: Red Spells Danger could get an easy lead if rivals are too respectful early, allowing him to control the race completely
Watch if Soda gets too far back early as she'll need the leaders to come back to her in a small field
Tip Foster's market support will indicate connections' confidence in post-gelding improvement
Sparkling Wine's fitness after such a long break is a major unknown despite the capable Dods yard
Early positioning will be crucial as prominent runners Red Spells Danger, Tip Foster and Rousham establish the early order

races.name: Traditional Family Day Sunday 17th May Handicap

runners_data.name: Miss Mambo
runners_data.note: Prominent style but recent form suggests racing in midfield, handicap debut gives realistic chance despite trainer's poor 14-day record
runners_data.comment: Showed some ability in maidens and she needs watching in market on handicap debut
runners_data.spotlight: Showed some ability in maidens, including when third of six at Bath (1m, good to soft) three weeks ago; this is more realistic on handicap debut and she's a half-sister to four winners; needs watching in market.

runners_data.name: Masaban
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who showed ability in Ireland before gelding, stable debut suggests more needed but has scope for improvement
runners_data.comment: Unexposed gelding and he looks interesting upped to 1m on handicap debut; watch market
runners_data.spotlight: Signs of ability in two runs for Dermot Weld last summer (7f, yielding/1m, AW); gelded and sold for 20,000euros in November; finished sixth of 14 on stable debut at Doncaster (6f, good to firm) last month but he made some late headway and that was promising after 252 days off; should benefit from that run and he looks interesting back up in trip on handicap debut.

runners_data.name: Clear Above
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who has been disappointing in handicaps, another ratings drop but needs significant improvement to be competitive
runners_data.comment: 0-5 and he's been well held in both handicaps; needs improvement back on turf
runners_data.spotlight: Five-race maiden who has not really progressed and he was well held in two handicaps (7/1m, Tapeta) last month; dropped another 3lb but he needs a transformation back on turf.

runners_data.name: Resdev Time
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who has failed to win in seven attempts, continues to slide down handicap but consistent level of form
runners_data.comment: Seven-race maiden who has not made an impact in four handicaps; needs to find more
runners_data.spotlight: Seven-race maiden who has not made an impact in four handicaps and was almost 3l behind Dalamara when fifth at Redcar (1m, good to firm) last month; continues to drop down the weights but she needs to raise her game.

runners_data.name: Bobbys Pride
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from 236-day break with fade-in-finish warning, still unexposed but long absence is concerning
runners_data.comment: Didn't show much as a 2yo and has lots to prove on her return
runners_data.spotlight: Struggled at big prices in all four 2yo runs, including a nursery at Musselburgh (1m, good to soft) in September; still unexposed but she's on the same mark as last time and has lots to prove on her return.

runners_data.name: Dalamara
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who won on AW debut then ran respectably at Redcar, consistent form gives each-way claims in tactical race
runners_data.comment: Won at Newcastle in December and creditable fourth at Redcar last month; shortlisted
runners_data.spotlight: Finished well when scoring at 16-1 on handicap debut at Newcastle (1m, AW) in December; never-dangerous fourth behind an emphatic winner at Redcar (1m, good to firm) last month but that was a creditable effort after a break and she still has potential; shortlisted.

runners_data.name: Hood Wink
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse carrying penalty after dead-heat win 12 days ago, good turn of foot shown but 7lb rise makes task harder
runners_data.comment: Off the mark when dead-heating at Wetherby last month; respected under a penalty
runners_data.spotlight: Off the mark at the tenth attempt when dead-heating in a Wetherby handicap (1m, good to firm) 12 days ago; this is tougher under a penalty but he showed a good attitude last time and is open to more progress; respected.

runners_data.name: Princess Coco
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with fade-in-finish warning, poor recent form makes her hard to recommend despite bottom weight
runners_data.comment: Has not shown much in her five starts, including a Redcar handicap last month; opposable
runners_data.spotlight: Half-sister to numerous winners but she's not shown much and was a long way behind two of today's rivals on handicap debut at Redcar last month; opposable.

races.paceDynamic: Miss Mambo is the most prominent early runner but she's been racing in midfield rather than genuine pace-setting, while Resdev Time has also shown prominent tendencies. With most runners preferring to sit back (Masaban, Clear Above, Dalamara, Hood Wink, Bobbys Pride, Princess Coco all hold-up types), this looks set to be a slowly-run affair with no genuine speed horses to force the issue. The lack of natural pace-setters will create a tactical crawl followed by a sprint finish over the final 2-3 furlongs. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses who can produce a turn of foot, as they'll get the slow early fractions they need to be effective.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is as slow as expected with Miss Mambo and Resdev Time failing to force it early
scenarios.body: The tactical nature will suit horses who can quicken from off the pace, with the in-form Hood Wink and consistent Dalamara best placed to exploit the sprint finish. Hold-up specialists get their ideal race scenario.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Press On
scenarios.trigger: If Miss Mambo or Resdev Time decide to make more use of their early speed than recent form suggests
scenarios.body: A more genuine pace would stretch the field and expose stamina limitations in some of the hold-up horses who prefer to sprint. The more resolute stayers among the field would benefit from a true test.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Penalty Backfires On Winner
scenarios.trigger: If Hood Wink cannot reproduce his Wetherby dead-heat form under his penalty
scenarios.body: The handicapper's 7lb rise for his breakthrough win proves too much, opening the door for lightly-weighted rivals. Bobbys Pride and Princess Coco get their chance at the bottom of the handicap.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Mess Creates Shock
scenarios.trigger: If jockeys get their tactics badly wrong in the slowly-run race and kick too late
scenarios.body: A muddling pace sees most runners in with chances turning for home but stamina becomes crucial in the final furlong. The longest-priced runners who stay strongly get their moment.

watchPoints.text: Hood Wink carries a 7lb penalty for his recent dead-heat win and may find the quick turnaround and weight rise too much
Miss Mambo and Resdev Time are the only pace angles but both have been racing more conservatively lately
Bobbys Pride returns from a 236-day absence which makes her fitness questionable despite the low weight
The slow early pace will create a bunched field turning for home with little between several runners
Dalamara showed a good attitude when winning on AW and ran respectably last time despite the emphatic winner

races.name: Dr Keith Howard OBE Memorial Handicap

runners_data.name: Le Beau Garcon
runners_data.note: Prominent racer returning from 221-day break with preference for faster ground than today's good going
runners_data.comment: Four wins at this trip and he has a good record when fresh; in the mix off workable mark
runners_data.spotlight: Handles most ground but all of his four wins have been on good to firm; last success was at Ayr (5f) 12 months ago but that was on his reappearance and he's only 1lb higher for today's return; needs a close look after 221 days off.

runners_data.name: Glory Fighter
runners_data.note: Proven front-runner who made all last time and suits this tactical setup with moderate early pace
runners_data.comment: Recorded his 11th win when making all at Nottingham; respected off 2lb higher
runners_data.spotlight: Admirable veteran who recorded his 11th win when making all at Nottingham (5f, good) last month; there wasn't much separating the first five but he's only 2lb higher here and should give it another good shot.

runners_data.name: Betweenthesticks
runners_data.note: In-form prominent racer with two recent wins who handles good ground well and suited by 5f distance
runners_data.comment: Has won his last two starts and yard won this in 2023 and 2025; key player
runners_data.spotlight: Returned from six months off with a win at Wolverhampton and he followed up with another narrow success at Pontefract (5f, good) 17 days ago; 3lb higher than for his front-running win last time but remains feasibly treated and is tactically versatile; key player for yard that won this in 2023 and 2025.

runners_data.name: Hurt You Never
runners_data.note: Prominent racer struggling for form since August double, needs to prove fitness after disappointing recent runs
runners_data.comment: Prolific winner but she's lost her way and needs to turn things around
runners_data.spotlight: Prolific winner who is on a dangerous mark but she's been out of sorts since completing a double at Hamilton (5f, good) last August; has plenty to prove and needs to turn things around back in trip.

runners_data.name: Impressor
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who prefers softer ground and may find today's good surface too fast for optimal performance
runners_data.comment: On last winning mark but he's been well held in his last two starts; down the list
runners_data.spotlight: Eight-time sprint winner who is suited by good to soft or slower; his last success was off this mark in September but he's been well held at Musselburgh (5f) and Thirsk (6f) in his two runs; has bit to prove again and wouldn't want the ground to dry out.

runners_data.name: Mark's Choice
runners_data.note: Course specialist hold-up horse returning from poor Thirsk reappearance, needs strong pace to be effective
runners_data.comment: Ten-time course winner who is not ruled back at this track on his second run after a break
runners_data.spotlight: Ten-time course winner who ended last season with two wins (6f/5f) at Ripon; struggled on Thirsk reappearance last month but he doesn't have a great record when fresh and he's not ruled out back at his favoured track; acts on good to firm and soft.

runners_data.name: Wrestling Revenue
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer on low weight but poor recent form suggests he needs significant improvement to feature
runners_data.comment: Won at Pontefract in October but he's been out of sorts in three subsequent runs
runners_data.spotlight: Turned things around with a win at Pontefract (5f, good) in October but he's been back in the doldrums in three subsequent runs; has plenty to prove again and needs another bolt from the blue.

runners_data.name: Vince L'Amour
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner wearing tongue-tie who disappointed over course and distance 13 days ago despite improved Musselburgh second
runners_data.comment: Hard to predict and was last of eight over C&D two weeks ago; others preferred
runners_data.spotlight: Returned to form with a second at Musselburgh (5f, good to soft) last month but he failed to back that up over C&D (last of eight) two weeks ago; has something to prove again after that and he's still 3lb higher than for his last win.

runners_data.name: He's An Angel
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer on very low weight but poor record on turf and 27 days since last run counts against
runners_data.comment: Frequent slow starter and he has work to do from out of the weights back in trip
runners_data.spotlight: Hold-up performer who scored at Wolverhampton (6f, AW) in January but he's not hit the same level since and was always behind after a slow start at Southwell last month; comes with risks attached and he will need a good pace back at this trip; 2lb out of the weights.

races.paceDynamic: With only Vince L'Amour showing genuine front-running tendencies and several prominent racers like Glory Fighter, Betweenthesticks, and Le Beau Garcon likely to press forward, this shapes as a moderately contested early pace. The speed won't be fierce given the limited natural pace in the field, allowing tactical positioning battles to develop through the first three furlongs. Hold-up horses like Mark's Choice, Impressor, and He's An Angel will find themselves with work to do if the pace becomes too sedate. This race shape favours prominent racers who can track the early leader and kick when the pace lifts, rather than pure front-runners or hold-up specialists.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent racers dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Glory Fighter or Betweenthesticks can track Vince L'Amour and maintain striking position
scenarios.body: The moderate early pace allows these proven 5f specialists to conserve energy before unleashing their finishing kicks in the final furlong. Their recent form and tactical speed proves decisive over both pure pace-setters and hold-up horses arriving too late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-runner steals march
scenarios.trigger: If Vince L'Amour gets an uncontested lead and the pace becomes too slow early
scenarios.body: The lack of genuine pace pressure allows him to dictate terms completely, building an unassailable advantage before the field can react. His tactical speed from the front proves more effective than his recent poor form suggested.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-up surge succeeds
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace collapses completely and becomes crawling slow
scenarios.body: Mark's Choice and Impressor benefit from their patient tactics as the race becomes a sprint from the 2f pole. Their class and finishing kicks overwhelm horses who went too early in the changed race dynamic.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace collapse causes chaos
scenarios.trigger: If no horse commits to making the running and the field clusters together
scenarios.body: The lack of early pace creates a bunched field where positioning and racing room become crucial, favouring horses with tactical pace who can quicken from any position. Traffic problems eliminate several leading chances.

watchPoints.text: Glory Fighter could dominate if allowed to dictate from the front as he did when winning at Nottingham last time out
Mark's Choice's poor Thirsk reappearance suggests he may need this run despite being a course specialist with two wins here last season
Betweenthesticks carries headgear changes with a pulling wind and may race more aggressively than his recent settled tactics suggest
The good ground may disadvantage Impressor who has shown his best form on softer surfaces throughout his career
Wrestling Revenue drops significantly in grade on a low weight but his poor recent form makes him hard to trust despite the conditions

races.name: Sam Alexander Memorial Handicap

runners_data.name: First Folio
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning from 184-day break with solid Yarmouth course form but needs to prove fitness first time back
runners_data.comment: Yarmouth specialist who has not won since September 2024; looks opposable on return
runners_data.spotlight: All of his four wins have been at Yarmouth (6f, good/good to firm) and latest was in September 2024; well treated on old form but he had a mixed record last season and was well held in the autumn on his final two runs; has a bit to prove after six months off and others are preferred.

runners_data.name: Modern Times
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with excellent recent form including creditable fifth here last month, suits the expected pace scenario perfectly
runners_data.comment: C&D winner who has posted two solid efforts this season; shouldn't be far away
runners_data.spotlight: Won a C&D maiden (good) last June on his second start for Tim Easterby; returned after a lengthy absence with a creditable fifth here (6f, good to soft) last month and ran another solid race at Pontefract last time; still looks on a workable mark and he shouldn't be far away.

runners_data.name: It Just Takes Time
runners_data.note: Prominent type who has faded in both runs this season and faces a dangerous handicap mark after 2023 success
runners_data.comment: Finished down the field in last three runs and latest was over C&D three weeks ago
runners_data.spotlight: C&D winner in 2023 but all his subsequent wins have come over 7f+; on dangerous mark but he's faded at big prices in both runs this season and latest was over C&D (eighth of 16) three weeks ago; down the list.

runners_data.name: Musical Touch
runners_data.note: Strong closer who won at Thirsk last spring and returned with AW success, up 4lb but handicapper may have been lenient
runners_data.comment: Won on Southwell reappearance last month; up 4lb but he's a big player again back on turf
runners_data.spotlight: Acts on good to firm and soft ground; won at Thirsk (6f, good) last spring and recorded his second AW win on his Southwell reappearance last month; up 4lb but he still looks feasibly treated and should get a good tow into this race; key player.

runners_data.name: Fortamour
runners_data.note: Prominent runner and six-time course winner but well held in three runs this year, past course form gives him claims
runners_data.comment: Has good record in this race in recent years but needs a major revival
runners_data.spotlight: Six-time course winner but well held in his three runs this year and latest was over C&D (good to soft) last month; has form figures of 1242 in this race in the last four years but he needs to turn things around off a sliding mark.

runners_data.name: Grant Wood
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with two Newcastle wins earlier this year but needs to step up after disappointing eighth last time
runners_data.comment: Began this year with two Newcastle wins but was disappointing there latest; risks attached
runners_data.spotlight: Began this year with two Newcastle wins (6f, Tapeta) but he was only eighth of ten there last month; has won over C&D but has a patchy profile and needs to step up again on this return to turf.

runners_data.name: Charlie Mason
runners_data.note: Closer whose five wins have all been at this trip, disappointing favorite last time but only 1lb higher today
runners_data.comment: Disappointing favourite at Doncaster latest and this is a step back up in grade
runners_data.spotlight: All five wins have been this trip but he had a near-miss over 5f at Wolverhampton in March; only 1lb higher today but he was a disappointing favourite back on turf at Doncaster (5f, good to soft) last time; has a bit to prove again after that and this is a step back up in grade.

runners_data.name: U Sure Do
runners_data.note: Prominent type with excellent turf record including two Catterick wins last season, 6lb higher than last success
runners_data.comment: Two wins last season and was good fourth on his Thirsk reappearance last month; in the mix
runners_data.spotlight: All 12 runs have been on turf and he won twice at Catterick (6f/7f, good) last season; 6lb higher than for his last success but he reappeared with a creditable fourth of 13 at Thirsk last month; should benefit from that run and he's in the mix on this drop back in trip; tongue-tie added.

runners_data.name: Beyond Borders
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who scored off higher mark at Yarmouth last June but hasn't approached that form since
runners_data.comment: Won at Yarmouth last June but he's struggled since and has plenty to prove; new headgear
runners_data.spotlight: Scored off 3lb higher at Yarmouth (6f, good) last June but he's not come close to that form since and was seventh of nine on Leicester reappearance last month; plenty to prove and four of his five wins were as 2yo; cheekpieces added.

runners_data.name: Wreck It Ryley
runners_data.note: Closer who hit personal best at Leicester last month but flopped off revised mark 12 days later
runners_data.comment: Won by 6l at Leicester last month but flopped on his return visit 12 days later
runners_data.spotlight: 6yo who hit a personal best with his emphatic win at Leicester (6f, good) last month but he flopped off this revised mark there 12 days later; has won at Ripon but he's not easy to predict and needs to bounce back again after that last run.

runners_data.name: Novamay
runners_data.note: Front runner with three consecutive turf wins last July including course success, returning after 239-day absence
runners_data.comment: Three turf wins last summer and she could have more to offer as a 4yo; respected on return
runners_data.spotlight: Won three in a row on turf (6f, good) last July and the first leg was over C&D; went up 25lb but she ended last season with a creditable fourth on AW at Newcastle; could have more to offer as a 4yo and needs a close look on her return.

races.paceDynamic: Novamay provides the only confirmed early speed in this field and will set a comfortable tempo without pressure from the break. The prominent runners First Folio, It Just Takes Time, Fortamour and U Sure Do will track behind but none are aggressive pace-pressers. This creates a measured rhythm that allows the hold-up brigade including Modern Times, Musical Touch, Grant Wood, Charlie Mason, Beyond Borders and Wreck It Ryley plenty of time to organize. The sustainable pace and lack of early pressure strongly favors closers who can time their runs in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Closer's Paradise
scenarios.trigger: If Novamay sets uncontested fractions and the pace stays honest throughout
scenarios.body: The moderate tempo allows hold-up horses to get into perfect striking positions and unleash late kicks. Modern Times and Musical Touch have the class to capitalize on this scenario with their proven finishing speed.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds
scenarios.trigger: If Novamay builds an unassailable lead and the closers leave their runs too late
scenarios.body: The mare gets first run on tired legs behind her and holds off late challenges. Her three consecutive wins last season prove she can sustain strong pace when allowed easy fractions.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent runners position perfectly and kick before the hold-up horses react
scenarios.body: First Folio or It Just Takes Time use their tactical speed to bridge the gap between Novamay and the back markers. Their ability to race handily gives them first jump on the deeper closers.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Sprint Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses completely and it becomes a pure sprint finish over the final furlong
scenarios.body: Charlie Mason's 5f speed comes into play despite the 6f trip, while Grant Wood's recent Newcastle form suggests sharp acceleration. The race becomes about pure finishing kick rather than sustained speed.

watchPoints.text: Novamay's fitness after 239 days off could see her stop quickly if the layoff has taken its toll
Modern Times and Musical Touch both show strong recent form that suggests they're primed for big efforts
First Folio's 184-day absence makes his fitness a major question mark despite solid historical course form
Grant Wood's inconsistent profile means he could either bounce back strongly or disappoint again
The lack of early pace pressure could see several hold-up horses finishing strongly and bunching up late

races.name: Napoleons Casino And Restaurant Leeds Handicap

runners_data.name: Garden Oasis
runners_data.note: Only front runner with seven Ripon wins but 11-year-old faces wall of closers
runners_data.comment: Seven-time course winner who was second at Pontefract latest; respected back up in trip
runners_data.spotlight: 14-time winner including seven times at Ripon; his last success was off 5lb higher last summer and he returned to form with a second at Pontefract (1m, good) last month; hasn't run over this far for a long time but he used to be effective at this trip and most of his wins have been in May-August.

runners_data.name: Dawn Of Liberation
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse perfectly suited to this pace scenario with strong 1m2f record
runners_data.comment: Three wins last summer but he's been quiet in two runs this season; needs to step up
runners_data.spotlight: Five-time winner, three times at around 1m2f (good/good to firm) last summer; well handicapped on his best form last season but he's been quiet in two runs this spring and needs to rediscover his spark.

runners_data.name: Glistening Nights
runners_data.note: Prominent runner faces traffic dangers but all five wins came at this trip
runners_data.comment: Placed in a Class 4 over C&D on his reappearance last month; each-way claims again
runners_data.spotlight: All five wins have been at around 1m2f on good or quicker; last success was off 5lb lower but he reappeared with a fair third in Class 4 event over C&D (good to soft) last month; should go well on this drop back in grade and it would be a positive if the ground dries out.

runners_data.name: Poet's Dawn
runners_data.note: Prominent style risky here but back to last winning mark for in-form Easterby yard
runners_data.comment: 12-time turf winner who is on last winning mark and could be dangerous back up in trip
runners_data.spotlight: 12-time turf winner including over C&D; hasn't made a serious impact in his two runs (1m) this season but he's now back on last winning mark and could be dangerous back up in trip; one of three runners for the yard.

runners_data.name: Triple Force
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning from 162-day break but had excellent turf campaign last year
runners_data.comment: Four wins on turf last season and could find more progress as 5yo; interesting contender
runners_data.spotlight: Had a highly productive time on turf last season including four wins (1m1f/1m2f) and four seconds; struggled in his hat-trick bid in November but that was on AW and he still looks feasibly treated on his penultimate form; interesting contender who needs a close look on return.

runners_data.name: Bass Player
runners_data.note: Hold-up style suits but 122-day absence and poor recent Wolverhampton form concern
runners_data.comment: Had a major blip at Wolverhampton in January and needs to bounce back after wind surgery
runners_data.spotlight: First win was on turf (7f) and last two have been on Tapeta (8.6f); reached the frame in two starts at Wolverhampton in December but he had a major blip there the following month; had another wind operation since and needs a major revival after four months off.

runners_data.name: No Knee Never
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with penalty after Wolverhampton win but solid turf form
runners_data.comment: Clearcut win at Wolverhampton last time and he's respected under a penalty
runners_data.spotlight: Rarely runs a bad race and he's won two of his last three starts, including an emphatic win at Wolverhampton (8.6f, AW) 11 days ago; has a penalty back on turf but he ran right up to his best last time and this new trip should be within range; respected.

runners_data.name: Jewel Maker
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse struggling with slow starts this season needs to improve dramatically
runners_data.comment: 12-time winner but he's lost his way and needs to turn things around
runners_data.spotlight: Veteran with 12 wins but he's lost his way and has struggled after slow starts in both runs this spring; has something to prove and he needs to turn things around back up in trip.

runners_data.name: Nanny Park
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner who struggled on stable debut but suited to this developing pace
runners_data.comment: Just one win from 11 starts and she struggled on stable debut last month; down the list
runners_data.spotlight: 1m AW winner for James Fanshawe as 2yo and ran some good races last year off higher marks than this; has form at up to 1m3f but struggled on stable debut at Doncaster last month and needs to leave that form well behind.

runners_data.name: Velvet Whisper
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with strong 1m2f+ record but 26 days since last run
runners_data.comment: Ended last year with two wins; well held on return but she could still have more to offer
runners_data.spotlight: Relatively lightly raced 4yo who ended last year with wins at Nottingham (1m2f, heavy) and Musselburgh (1m4f, soft); started this season with a low-key effort but she may have needed that run and still has scope for further progress; not ruled out dropped back in trip and grade.

runners_data.name: Star Cast
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with AW penalty but lightly raced on turf and improving rapidly
runners_data.comment: 4yo who found more progress when winning at Newcastle last week; respected back on turf
runners_data.spotlight: Three wins on AW at Newcastle (1m2f) since January including a cosy success last Friday; this is tougher under a penalty but she's still lightly raced on turf and was third in a big field at Doncaster (1m, good to soft) on her penultimate run; shortlisted.

runners_data.name: Tiberio Force
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning from 158-day break and 6lb out of handicap proper
runners_data.comment: Infrequent winner and this is tough from out of the weights on his return; opposable
runners_data.spotlight: Has gained both wins on turf, three years apart; his last success was over C&D last summer but he was well held in final three runs last year; 6lb out of the weights on his return and best watched in this competitive race.

races.paceDynamic: Garden Oasis will set a comfortable tempo with only Glistening Nights, Poet's Dawn, Triple Force, No Knee Never, Velvet Whisper and Tiberio Force wanting prominent positions early. The single leader creates sustainable fractions but the prominent pack of six creates serious traffic problems turning into the straight over this 1m2f trip. With Dawn Of Liberation, Bass Player, Jewel Maker, Nanny Park and Star Cast all held up, there's a wall of horses coming from behind down Ripon's testing straight. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses who can find clear runs and use their finishing kick.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent pack creates traffic problems as expected in the straight
scenarios.body: Garden Oasis sets honest pace but gets swamped by closers finding daylight down the outside. The backmarkers time their runs perfectly while the prominent group gets shuffled back.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Position Pays
scenarios.trigger: If one of the prominent horses finds the perfect stalking position without traffic
scenarios.body: Triple Force or No Knee Never avoids the congestion and kicks clear while others get stuck behind faltering leaders. Their tactical speed proves decisive over this distance.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Staying Power Required
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes genuinely strong and tests stamina reserves
scenarios.body: Garden Oasis gets company and they go too fast early, setting up a war of attrition. The proven stayers with form over 1m2f+ come to the fore in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If Garden Oasis gets an uncontested lead and the field comes too late
scenarios.body: The 14-time winner uses his Ripon experience to dictate terms and kick clear approaching the final furlong. His class tells when the pressure comes and he holds on grimly.

races.name: Ripon Races Ladies Day 18th June Handicap

runners_data.name: Laser Luck
runners_data.note: Non-runner
runners_data.comment: 0-8 and well held when upped to this trip at Beverley last month; down the list
runners_data.spotlight: Eight-race maiden who has form figures of 60555 in handicaps for her current yard and was well held when upped to this trip at Beverley (good to firm) last month; others preferred.

runners_data.name: Lady Vanguard
runners_data.note: Another confirmed leader who showed promise on handicap debut but 27 days off is a slight concern
runners_data.comment: Ran well for long way on handicap debut at Yarmouth (1m); player if she can build on that
runners_data.spotlight: 320,000gns yearling; didn't show much in three qualifying runs but she ran well for a long way when fourth on handicap debut at Yarmouth (1m, good) last month; needs to build on that but it's still early days and she's open to more progress at this new trip.

runners_data.name: Port Darwin
runners_data.note: Front runner with decent recent form but needs to prove he can see out this trip under pressure
runners_data.comment: Turf winner last summer and runner-up at Kempton last week; in the mix back in trip
runners_data.spotlight: Record of 1-10 but his win was off 4lb higher at Musselburgh (1m, good) last August; mixed record since but he returned to form with a clear second in first-time blinkers at Kempton (1m4f) last week; has claims if he can back that up and he's in the mix back in trip.

runners_data.name: Mereside Princess
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who consistently hits the frame and the step up in trip should suit
runners_data.comment: 0-11 but she's on a reduced mark and could go well if she settles at this new trip
runners_data.spotlight: 11-race maiden but she's reached the frame in five handicaps including when fourth at Wetherby (1m, good to firm) last month; can take a strong hold but she continues to edge down the weights and could be a factor if she's settles at this new trip; blinkers reapplied.

runners_data.name: Evergreen Emerald
runners_data.note: First-time handicapper after 226 days off, needs watching for market support but has ability concerns
runners_data.comment: Masar filly who is a possible improver upped to 1m2f on handicap debut; market useful
runners_data.spotlight: Masar filly who was well held in three 2yo runs at around 7f but this is more realistic and she's a possible improver upped in trip on handicap debut; needs watching in market back from 226 days off.

runners_data.name: Heated Moment
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner who faded badly when tried over this trip last time, questionable stamina
runners_data.comment: Six-race maiden who has not finished closer than 5l to a winner; down the list
runners_data.spotlight: Six-race maiden who has not finished closer than 5l to a winner and was a fading fifth when upped to 1m2f on stable debut at Yarmouth (good) last month; mark continues to fall but she needs to find improvement from somewhere.

runners_data.name: Bradbury
runners_data.note: Most progressive type with tongue-tie fitted, the step up from 1m4f to 1m2f suits his closing style
runners_data.comment: Unexposed gelding who was an eye-catching fourth at Wolverhampton; respected back in trip
runners_data.spotlight: Unexposed gelding who ran into some trouble before finishing well for fourth in a Wolverhampton handicap (1m4f; tongue-tie added) 11 days ago; looks interesting off the same mark and this drop back in trip should be fine on pedigree (half-brother to two winners at up to 9.5f).

runners_data.name: Riddikulus
runners_data.note: Consistent place-getter but 83 days off makes her hard to assess for improvement
runners_data.comment: Has good pedigree but she's not progressed so far and has been well held in both handicaps
runners_data.spotlight: Half-sister to a fairly useful winner (1m/1m2f) but she's not really progressed so far and has been beaten around 8l in both handicaps; returns after a short break and she needs improvement back up in trip.

runners_data.name: Vietnorm
runners_data.note: Gelded since last run but poor form figures suggest he's up against it here
runners_data.comment: Well held at big prices in all five runs; gelded and steps up to 1m2f on return
runners_data.spotlight: Well held at big prices in three qualifying runs and same story when sixth of eighth on handicap debut at Wolverhampton (8.6f) in December; gelded since but he's needs to show a lot more at this new trip on his return.

runners_data.name: Fuzeyya
runners_data.note: Struggled in longer trips this season, the drop back from 1m4f could help but form is poor
runners_data.comment: Has struggled in four of her five runs and needs a transformation back on turf
runners_data.spotlight: Showed some ability in a Bath maiden (1m, good to soft) last September but she's struggled in her four other runs, including two AW handicaps (1m4f/1m2f) this spring; has lots to prove and needs a transformation back on turf; cheekpieces worn in last three runs are removed.

races.paceDynamic: Port Darwin and Lady Vanguard will contest the early lead, with Port Darwin likely to get first run having shown better tactical speed recently. The honest gallop they set should create a genuine test over this staying trip on good ground. With most of the field holding up (Bradbury, Mereside Princess, Heated Moment all backmarkers), there's a clear divide between pace setters and closers. This race shape strongly favours the prominent runners and those with tactical pace, as the kick from the back will come too late against a solid early tempo.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front runner holds on
scenarios.trigger: If Port Darwin or Lady Vanguard get an easy lead and aren't pressed hard early
scenarios.body: The leaders get breathing space to establish rhythm before the back markers can mount their challenge. The long run-in isn't enough to peg back a horse with first run from the front.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late closer strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely strong between the two leaders
scenarios.body: The sustained gallop sets up perfectly for the hold-up horses who have stamina for this trip. Bradbury's recent Wolverhampton form and step up in trip could prove decisive.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace collapses scenario
scenarios.trigger: If both leaders go too fast early and tie up in the final two furlongs
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint finish where any horse with a turn of foot can capitalize. The midfield runners get the perfect setup to sweep past tired leaders.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the market principals underperform and an unconsidered runner finds improvement
scenarios.body: Evergreen Emerald's first try at this trip or Vietnorm's return from a break catches the field napping. The pace scenario matters less as class levels prove closer than expected.
